parameters.note: How far back each Apple Health read looks for scale weigh-ins (K-402): the trend's own window (trend_display_days, windows.yaml), so a scale that synced late still lands inside the trend it changes. Older history is an import (K-609). Each sample keeps its Health id as its clientId: reading it again stores nothing twice.

How far back the one-time import of Apple Health weigh-ins reads (K-616, ADR-018 §3): a year of history, enough for the trend and the strength of a habit, not a lifetime. It ends where the regular read (health_weight_read_days) begins; a sample both ever read is stored once, by its Health id (the first to store it keeps its source). Imported weigh-ins are seen in the trend and never read by the engine (ADR-053).

The weigh-in chart's longer view, 'Year' (K-616, ADR-018 §3 'the history is seen at once'): as far back as an import reads (health_weight_import_days), so what was brought in can be seen. The copy says 'Year'; a change here changes that word too.
The weigh-in screen's chart (K-402): the longest decision window (women, 28 days, decision_window_days in windows.yaml), so the weeks a call is made on are always in sight.

How far back each Apple Health read looks for steps, sleep and active energy (K-404): the longest decision window (women, 28 days, decision_window_days), since a week's step days are judged in it (K-220). A day already sent with the same values is not sent again.

The Apple Health workouts that count as cardio done (K-959, ADR-074 #6): steady cardio, the low-tempo kind the coaching prescribes (K-33; ADR-074 #2 names cycling, incline walking, elliptical). HKWorkoutActivityType raw values: 13 cycling, 16 elliptical, 24 hiking, 35 rowing, 37 running, 44 stair climbing, 46 swimming, 52 walking, 60 cross-country skiing, 68 stairs, 69 step training, 70 wheelchair walk pace, 71 wheelchair run pace, 73 mixed cardio, 74 hand cycling. Not counted: intervals (63 HIIT, 64 jump rope, 30 mixed metabolic cardio; K-34: HIIT is not prescribed), strength (50, the app's own sessions), sports and mind-body.
